reason: The hypothesis relies on the formation of γ′ precipitates via Al/Ti additions and the resulting high-temperature strength, which are directly supported by E1. The baseline cryogenic toughness of FCC HEAs is supported by E1 and E2. However, the claimed improvements in environmental resistance and radiation tolerance are not addressed by any cited evidence, leaving two key premises unsupported.
premises: FCC HEAs have low yield strength (~200 MPa as-cast) that limits structural use
Adding Al+Ti to an FCC HEA matrix can form an ordered L12 γ′ precipitate phase
A γ+γ′ dual-phase HEA exhibits excellent thermal stability, coarsening resistance, and strength retention around 800°C
The γ′ phase in Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Al-Ti HEAs has near-stoichiometric composition (Ni,Co)3(Ti,Al) and depends on Al+Ti content
FCC HEAs show extraordinary ductility and fracture toughness at ambient and cryogenic temperatures
